answer.rationale: The p99 latency degradation (5x target) on the write path is confined to the primary region and coincides precisely with a release 2 hours ago. memory_b1 demonstrates that rollback has successfully cleared checkout errors without customer impact in prior incidents. memory_b6 shows staged release gating catches regressions quickly. The release timing correlation is strong. A rollback is the fastest available lever to isolate whether the recent build caused the write path regression, and it preserves the ability to investigate further if latency persists. During settlement peak with heavy writes, rollback carries lower risk than adding capacity (which may not address root cause) or circuit breakers (which would degrade availability). Regional failover is valuable but slower to execute and doesn't isolate the release hypothesis. This is staged as small_guarded_test to monitor recovery before full commitment.
